# `element` declares its events, so codegen reads the declaration rather than
# matching names: which listener is attached, whether it takes an event
# argument, and what that argument stands for all come from there.
#
# Before, three name lists disagreed. An event outside click/input/change was
# routed to a registration that binds no event parameter, and the emitted
# signature was picked by a separate `event == "input" || event == "change"`
# test — so `@error(e) { msg = e.message }` compiled to a listener with no `e`
# and the body threw ReferenceError. On the lowered (JS-built) path a fourth
# list dropped any event outside click/input/change/submit on the floor.

sngl generate --platform html --lang none -o out events.sngl

# @error carries ErrorEvent, whose fields the element declares nothing of, so
# the parameter stands for the event and the listener takes it.
grep 'addEventListener\("error", function\(e\) \{' out/index.html
grep 'state\.msg = e\.message;' out/index.html
! grep 'addEventListener\("error", function\(\)' out/index.html

# @input carries InputEvent{value}, and `value` IS a prop of the element: the
# field is the control's own state, read back off the target.
grep 'addEventListener\("input", function\(e\) \{' out/index.html
grep 'state\.txt = e\.target\.value;' out/index.html

# A handler that declares no parameter gets no argument in the signature —
# the body has nothing that could resolve to the event.
grep 'addEventListener\("click", function\(\) \{' out/index.html

# An event the element declares no payload for still reaches its own DOM
# event through the wildcard event, and not click's listener.
grep 'addEventListener\("mouseover", function\(\) \{' out/index.html

# The same holds on the lowered path, where the element is built by JS: the
# listener is attached inside the slot renderer rather than dropped.
grep 'addEventListener\("mouseover", \(\) => \{' out/index.html

-- events.sngl --
import . "sngl://std"

component main {
    var msg string = ""
    var txt string = ""
    var hits int = 0
    var rows list<string> = ["a"]

    window {
        html.img(src = "x.png", @error(e) { msg = e.message })
        html.input(@input(e) { txt = e.value })
        html.button(@click { hits = hits + 1 })
        html.div(@mouseover { hits = hits + 1 })
        for r = rows {
            html.li(textContent = r, @mouseover { hits = hits + 1 })
        }
    }
}
